what:
Cursor plan refinements from 2026-04-23 clarification round (supplements memories #329 + #331 + #328 + #330).

**(1) Shared-rules + shared-MCP refactor — NEW DECISION.** Today each editor has a near-duplicate rule template. Refactor to: `src/templates/rules/shared/body.md` (identical tool-use guidance across editors) + `src/templates/rules/shared/layer-guidance.md` + per-editor `frontmatter` stubs + `_editor-notes.md.hbs` for editor-specific caveat inserts. `buildRules(adapter) = frontmatter + sharedBody + editorNotes`. One change in shared body → 5 editors updated. Same pattern for MCP: canonical `MCP_SERVER` spec + adapter transforms for envelope differences (Cursor requires `type: "stdio"` + `${workspaceFolder}` interpolation; Claude Code infers transport + takes absolute path). Skills: not needed for 0.5.0 but same pattern applies if we ever add them. This landed as addition to the CURSOR_ONBOARDING plan §3.

**(2) aide_remember tool-call chrome IS the correction-stored visibility channel in Cursor.** When agent calls aide_remember after a correction, Cursor shows the MCP tool call in standard chat chrome — user sees "aide_remember was called with what=..." just like any MCP tool call. Auto-approve setting affects whether user actively approves, but the call is always visible in transcript. No separate "correction was stored" notification needed. Per-editor docs state: "scroll up and look for the aide_remember tool call to confirm the correction was stored." Answer to the open question "how does user know correction was stored?" — already answered by MCP chrome, no workaround needed.

**(3) Rules-file regeneration risk mitigations (Phase C4).**
- Stale content risk: unit tests for every regen trigger path + backstop regen on `aide-memory init --force` + `aide-memory sync import`.
- Other rules files affected: none. Self-contained at `.cursor/rules/aide-memory.mdc`.
- Token-budget collision with user's own rules: `aide-memory init` WARNS if cumulative `alwaysApply: true` content across all .cursor/rules/*.mdc exceeds ~2000 tokens. Documented soft limit.
- Concurrent writes: atomic write via tmp + rename in `src/memory/rulesGen.ts`.
- Mid-session regen lag: Cursor reloads rules every turn — next turn picks up new content without restart. Documented in per-editor doc.
- Divergence from Claude Code SessionStart: both use same `buildSessionStartContent(store, config)` function. Single source, two consumers. No divergence by construction.

**(4) Release action is UNPUBLISH (not deprecate) + agent-driven source audit.** Per HANDOFF_MINIFIED_PUBLISH.md: aide-memory meets the 3-condition exception for CLI unpublish past the 72h window (no reverse deps + <300 weekly downloads + single maintainer). Unpublish pre-0.5.0 versions via `npm unpublish aide-memory@<version>` directly; do NOT just deprecate. Phase C9 source-audit checklist (agent runs):
  - Extract published tarball, grep for `.ts`, `.map`, `sourceMappingURL`, dev-manifest strings (`aide-v0`, `aide-legacy`, legacy dep names).
  - Grep bundles (`dist/cli/aide-memory.js`, `dist/memory/index.js`, `dist/memory/cli.js`) for readable original identifiers — function names from TS source like `detectCorrection`, `computeScopedForPath`, `maybeTriggerDriftResync` must NOT appear recognizably in minified output.
  - Manual spot-check first 200 lines of each bundle — expected format is shebang + single minified line.
  - INTENTIONALLY VISIBLE (not a leak): rules templates (`.md`/`.mdc`), `LICENSE.md`, `package.json`, `README.md`. User-facing content, not source code.

**(5) Per-phase validation gate mapping — apply memory #314 to every code-changing phase.** Each code-changing phase (C1-C6, C9) runs the full 10-check sequence from memory #314: npm build, 665+ unit tests, 4 bash smokes, e2e-autonomous, install-from-tarball, in-depth code review, full 17-step hook simulation against /tmp/aide-e2e, cursor-init-smoke (new for C2+), cursor-envelope tests (new for C3+), manual Claude Code walk to verify zero regression. Doc-only phases (C7, C8 internal parts) skip the code-change checks but still verify no broken links + correct cross-refs. Phase C8 validation run is itself the validation-gate execution. **Explicit anti-regression guard: every code-changing phase must prove Claude Code still works exactly as before.**
why: Five concrete refinements from the clarification round. Future sessions implementing Phases C1-C9 need these as constraints — especially (1) shared-rules refactor (prevents drift), (3) rules-regen mitigations (prevents subtle bugs), (4) source-audit checklist (prevents accidentally leaking code during 0.5.0 release), and (5) per-phase validation mapping (prevents Claude Code regressions during Cursor work). priority:always so they auto-inject on session start for every downstream Cursor-implementation session.
